A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DecAlign work. Their text, equations, five figures, seven tables, and Appendices A–C support a complete comparison; the shorter v3 retains the experimental and technical material.

before.justification: v2 reports original DecAlign benchmark results, component ablations, confusion matrices, modality-gap visualizations, and hyperparameter sensitivity results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including evaluations on CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, CH-SIMS, and six-class IEMOCAP.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same feature decoupling, prototype-guided transport, moment/MMD alignment, transformer fusion, and losses. The isolated re-expansion of CT in Section 4.2 is not accompanied by a changed algorithm or model.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four datasets, audiovisual/text modalities, English and Chinese sentiment tasks, and six-class emotion recognition task. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same 13 baselines. Tables 5–7 and Figure 3 also retain their respective comparator sets, including MCIS in Table 7. The removed references do not represent removed evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4, Appendix B, and the reproducibility statement retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, 50-epoch training budget, Adam optimizer, batch size of 32, and dataset-specific configurations. No new evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Table 2 retains the same ablation rows, and Figures 3–5 retain the confusion matrices, category analyses, modality-gap visualizations, and parameter sensitivity study. Appendix C preserves the corresponding analyses; the CT wording edit does not establish a revised experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five independent runs and specify seeds {1,2,3,4,5}. No uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or removed.

E6.justification: The matched numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged, including the appendix tables and ablations. For example, Table 1 retains DecAlign MAE values of 0.735 on MOSI and 0.543 on MOSEI, and CH-SIMS F1 of 81.85.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains Equations (1)–(13), including transport objectives, constraints, and alignment losses. Appendix B.5–B.6 retains the metric formulas and moment definitions. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about decoupled hierarchical alignment and superior performance across four benchmarks against 13 methods. Citation pruning does not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of complementary alignment roles, modality gaps, classification/regression behavior, and excessive alignment constraints remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix C. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added or removed.

D1.justification: The feature extraction details, Table 4 hyperparameters, A6000 hardware disclosure, reproducibility statement, project link, and code-release claims are retained. No implementation or access information is newly supplied.

R1.justification: v3 removes the broad application survey opening in Appendix A.1 and associated references, including medical and spatial applications. The introduction prunes visual-understanding citations and replaces AutoDrive-R2 with EMMA. The method-focused literature discussion and novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v3 shortens Appendix A.1 and replaces the Preprint header with the ICLR 2026 publication header. Section 4.2 changes one occurrence of 'Contrastive Training (CT)' to 'Cross-model Transformer (CT)'; the remaining narrative and section order are retained.

P2.justification: The figures, table structures, and captions are retained. Text reflow shifts existing displays and paragraph breaks, including Figure 3 and appendix tables, while the revised CT phrase is colored blue. There is no substantive visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly shortens broad background material while preserving the same method, evidence, and reproducibility information. Its isolated CT terminology correction leaves the contrastive-training explanations in Section 4.2 and Appendix C.3 unchanged, so that ambiguity remains unresolved. These limited editorial changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
